title: Beyond Static Observation Checklists: Dynamic Sequential Interaction Mapping for Assessing Trauma-Informed Teacher Competency and School Resilience in Disaster Education
content: Teacher preparation for trauma-informed disaster education typically depends on static observation checklists that overlook the rapid temporal dynamics linking student distress to educator responses. This study introduces a data-driven classroom observation framework—Sequential Interaction Mapping (SIM)—designed to extract micro-level temporal interaction patterns from high-fidelity video recordings of simulated earthquake drills in hazard-prone communities across West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. Through a Conversational Micro-Ethnographic Encoding Protocol, drill recordings are encoded frame by frame via a fine-tuned Vision-Language Transformer into two synchronized behavioral streams: student distress cues and educator interventions. Temporal lag matrices then estimate conditional probabilities of specific interventions occurring within a 0–10 second window after each distress cue, quantified via pointwise mutual information (PMI). A Gaussian mixture model clusters these lag profiles into five Adaptive Pedagogical Scripts representing empirically optimal cue–intervention sequences that minimize distress duration. These scripts are translated into behavioral indicators forming a PMI-weighted dynamic rubric matrix, where teacher competency is scored via cosine similarity between observed behavior vectors and script profiles to guide formative coaching and tiered certification. Continuously recalibrated with incoming drill data, SIM provides an empirically grounded, adaptive alternative to static expert-derived trauma-informed assessments.
